newsitem.title: UK: Blue Circle says no upturn in UK cement.
newsitem.headline: Blue Circle says no upturn in UK cement.

text.p: Britain's biggest cement producer Blue Circle Industries Plc said on Tuesday that UK cement demand shows "no significant signs of recovery," reflecting low investment in infrastructure and "weak new housing starts."

The company added that demand in the second half of 1996 is likely to compare more favourably with the same period a year before because the fall in demand started in mid-1995. Blue Circle's first half profit rose 12 percent to 116.3 million pounds ($181.8 million) from 104.1 million in 1995.
Interim dividend was increased to 4.25 pence per share from 4.0 pence.

The building materials group, whose profit and dividend increase were at the top end of analysts' expectations, said however that prospects for demand in its key overseas markets of the U.S., Chile and Malaysia "remain positive."
Trading conditions in another major overseas market, Nigeria, "remain difficult," Blue Circle added.
The company also said it sees "few signs of improvement" in its European Bathrooms and Heating businesses.
